pool.text: Explorer Gustav Adolf von Götzen passed through the village, recording it as Goma.
Congo Free State officers established a military outpost to oversee maritime activities on Lake Kivu.
This initiative culminated in the establishment of OPAC on February 4th.
Urbanization inception was formalized with the promulgation of a decree on February 21st.
Goma was elevated to the territorial and capital level of North Kivu.
North Kivu regained its district status on December 25th before becoming a region.
North Kivu attained regional autonomy on July 10th as a sovereign entity.
The Compagnie pour la Promotion des Activités Café was established and headquartered in the commune.
Nyiragongo erupted, sending a stream of lava through the center of the city.
Emissions from Nyiragongo volcano polluted surrounding areas of North Kivu with water vapor.
The intercultural ballet regularly participated in cultural events including the annual Goma Tourist Fair.
The Battle of Goma broke out in the city between the Congolese army and rebels.
The city was captured briefly by rebels of the March 23 Movement during rebellion.
Goma played host to the inaugural tshukudu race, a wooden bicycle race.
Festival Amani which celebrates peace attracted an audience of thirty-six thousand.
The Italian ambassador Luca Attanasio was killed in an apparent kidnapping attempt.
Goma was again targeted in a renewed offensive resulting in widespread casualties and displacement.
The Congolese government organized a national commemoration titled Résistance, Résilience et Unité.
